sentences.text:
Opposite Party
----
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rajesh Kumar
----
For the Petitioner(s)/Applicant(s) : Mr. Suraj Kishor Prasad, Adv.

For the State : Mr. Sunil Kr.
Dubey, A.P.P.
----
th 12/Dated: 12 April, 2024
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned counsel for the State.

2. The applicant who is in custody since 02.06.2022, has renewed his prayer for grant of regular bail in connection with S.T. Case No.27 of 2023 (arising out of Balumath P.S. Case No. 87/2022)
registered for the offence under Sections 498A, 304B and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, pending in the court of learned Additional Sessions Judge - II, Latehar.
3.
It appears that the applicant is accused of committing murder of his wife due to non-fulfilment of the demand of dowry.

4. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant(s) that complete set of FIR along with its enclosure have been annexed with this bail application and there is no suppression on his/her part.
5. Innocence has been claimed by the learned counsel for the applicant and undertaking has been given for participation in the trial.
On the above basis, prayer for bail has been made.

sentences.text: It has been informed by the learned counsel for the State that prosecution evidence has already been closed.
7. In that view of the matter, I am not inclined to reconsider the prayer for bail of the applicant.
Accordingly, the present bail application stands rejected.
8. However, the trial court is directed to expedite the trial or conclude the same as expeditiously as possible specifically considering the view that all the witnesses have been declared hostile.

(Rajesh Kumar, J.) Amar-A.S.K./-
